source.title: Map: the VIN-based parts shop for carlab.rs, full architecture spec
source.body:
## Destination

A full architecture spec for carlab.rs's real parts shop, ready to hand to implementation: VIN/model-based parts lookup (germsp.ru-style exploded-diagram ETK, starting with BMW), a part-identity/cross-reference data model spanning N suppliers (Intercars + our own warehouse + future suppliers), the fitment-data sourcing decision (paid TecDoc-like license vs build-by-hand vs supplier API), the core commerce platform choice (rebuilt Medusa vs an alternative, informed by research), per-supplier/warehouse markup with multi-source stock/price aggregation, Typesense search, a minimal admin (manual fitment curation running in parallel with whatever automatic source is found), cash+card payment (cash at pickup first, online card fast-follow), pickup first with delivery fast-follow, and ru/en/sr localization via the existing `@podbor/i18n` pattern.

**Acceptance:** no open decision blocks someone from starting to build. Every architectural fork below is either decided (see Notes) or has a research/grilling/task ticket in flight. This map does not carry execution — it ends at a spec, not working code (contrast with the old CarLab-Medusa map, #61, which did carry execution).

## Notes

**Domain:** `AGENTS.md`'s CarLab section, `docs/adr/0028-no-vehicle-dictionary-until-fitment-is-required.md`, `docs/adr/0034-pause-medusa-deploy-pending-shop-rebuild.md`, `docs/research/serbia-online-shop-legal.md` (the existing Serbian legal research — see "Accepted, not revisited" below). The old shop map is [#61](https://github.com/Zikrasoft/approved_rs/issues/61) (closed) — its 57-story spec (#77) and ADRs 0016–0027 describe the *abandoned* battery-only catalog+cart; this effort replaces it, not resumes it.

**Reference UX, studied live:** germsp.ru/etk (BMW ETK). VIN decodes to model/engine/trim with production-date and spec facts (oil volumes, paint code, etc). Catalog is organized as groups → exploded-diagram schemas with numbered callouts; each position is an OEM number + attributes (volume, "effective until" production-date cutoffs, gearbox/steering-side variant codes) + "see equivalents" (cross-reference/aftermarket numbers) + "see prices and availability", which expands into several lead-time tiers (70d/45d/16d/2-4d/1d/in-stock), each with its own price and quantity — and "in stock" splits further by region/warehouse with separate add-to-cart buttons. This is the shape carlab.rs is aiming to match, starting with consumables (germsp.ru's group=02). **Correction (from #323's research):** germsp.ru is an unrelated Russian importer, not an Intercars reseller — treat it as a UX/UI pattern to copy, not as evidence of how Intercars itself structures its data or pricing tiers.

**Standing decisions from the destination-pinning grilling session (2026-10-16), full rationale and the live Q&A in [Pin the destination and initial scope decisions](https://github.com/Zikrasoft/approved_rs/issues/321):**

- **Maximize ready-made.** Prefer an existing open-source/SaaS piece over hand-rolling, at every layer (platform, fitment data, VIN decode, search, payment) — custom code only where nothing fits. This is the standing tie-breaker for every research ticket below.
- **N-supplier architecture from day one**, not hardcoded to "Intercars + our warehouse". Each supplier/warehouse is a row with its own connector shape and its own markup %; adding a third supplier later is a new row, not a model change.
- **Part identity is layered, not one id.** OEM/factory number, manufacturer-brand aftermarket number, EAN, and each supplier's own article number are all different things pointing at the same physical part. Resolved as `Part` / `PartIdentifier` / `SupplierOffer` — see [GLOSSARY.md](https://github.com/Zikrasoft/approved_rs/blob/main/GLOSSARY.md), [ADR-0035](https://github.com/Zikrasoft/approved_rs/blob/main/docs/adr/0035-part-identity-one-canonical-part-brand-keyed-identifiers.md) and the gist in Decisions so far.
- **Fitment data: both paths in parallel, not sequenced.** An automatic source (paid license, alternative data vendor, or a supplier API that already carries fitment) and a manual hand-curation admin workflow are designed side by side from the start, each covering what the other doesn't — not "try automatic, fall back to manual only on failure".
- **Paid fitment-data licensing is on the table** (e.g. TecDoc-style) if the price is reasonable — research should price options, not restrict itself to free/open-source.
- **Markup is a per-warehouse/supplier %, editable in the admin.** No per-category/per-brand granularity at launch (fast-follow if ever needed).
- **Payment: cash at pickup/meeting first; online card payment is fast-follow**, designed in this spec but not required for launch.
- **Delivery: pickup-only first; delivery within Serbia is fast-follow**, same treatment as payment above.
- **Admin: prefer whatever admin ships with the chosen commerce platform** (e.g. Medusa's own admin) over building one from scratch. Day-one users are the owner plus 1-2 staff, one role, no RBAC needed yet.
- **Existing Serbian legal research is accepted as sufficient, by explicit owner choice** — `docs/research/serbia-online-shop-legal.md` is not being re-opened for online payment/fiscalization/delivery even though it explicitly left those out of scope when written for the old pickup-only/cash-only shop. This is a knowingly accepted gap, not a finding that the gap doesn't exist.
- **Old Medusa code stays in the repo for this map.** `apps/medusa`, `infra/medusa`, the old `apps/auto-service` shop pages are not deleted here — deletion is a task for implementation kickoff, once the new architecture is chosen, not part of this planning effort (point 12 of the owner's brief: this map is research + decisions only, no code changes).
- **Localization:** reuse `@podbor/i18n` (ru/en/sr) exactly as approved.rs/details.rs/carlab.rs already do. No new i18n mechanism — every new page/admin surface this spec produces plugs into the existing section-loader pattern.
- **Pilot:** start concretely with BMW (matches the germsp.ru reference studied live), roughly 2-liter engines, then automate outward to other German brands — the exact model/engine-code list is sharpened once the fitment-data research ([Fitment/TecDoc-like data source options](https://github.com/Zikrasoft/approved_rs/issues/324)) shows what's actually well covered.
- **Intercars relationship:** in-progress negotiation, preliminary green light — API research can proceed on a best-effort/public basis now; a task tracks getting real docs/sandbox access.

## Decisions so far

- [Pin the destination and initial scope decisions](https://github.com/Zikrasoft/approved_rs/issues/321): closed immediately after the destination-pinning grilling session — see the bullet list in Notes above for the gist of each standing decision; the ticket holds the full live Q&A.
- [Research: Intercars e-cat API capabilities](https://github.com/Zikrasoft/approved_rs/issues/323): Intercars runs a real public REST "IC API" (catalog, inventory/stock, pricing, sales, delivery, invoice), registered-client auth, pull/polling only (no webhooks), documented batch caps (100 SKUs / 10 warehouses per call). VIN/fitment is TecDoc-licensed through Intercars as a TecDoc consumer, not Intercars-proprietary — their own endpoints look like SKU/category search, not VIN search. Open questions for the access task (#328): exact auth/grant type, whether Serbia is live on the IC API vs CSV/legacy-only, real rate limits, and dropship-to-third-party-address support. Full findings in `docs/research/intercars-ecat-api.md` on branch `research/intercars-ecat-api`.
- [Research: online card payment (PSP) options for a Serbian shop](https://github.com/Zikrasoft/approved_rs/issues/326): **recommendation is CorvusPay and Monri WSPay**, get both on a call. CorvusPay is the only genuinely independent PSP with a published rate card (EUR 30/mo + 1.30%+EUR0.04 EEA / 3.20%+EUR0.04 non-EEA) and explicit Dina/DinaCard support; Monri, WSPay and NestPay all run on the same Payten/Asseco SEE infrastructure, Monri WSPay being the regional default with the broadest e-commerce-platform plugin ecosystem but unconfirmed Dina support. Stripe flatly rejects Serbian merchant entities; PayPal/Payoneer are cross-border-only, not confirmed to settle RSD locally, so neither is viable as the primary checkout. No PSP in this market publishes exact fees/settlement timing/onboarding docs — that needs a direct sales conversation, not more research. Full comparison in `docs/research/serbia-online-payment-psp.md` on branch `research/serbia-online-payment-psp`.
- [Research: ready-made / open-source options for a VIN-based parts shop](https://github.com/Zikrasoft/approved_rs/issues/322): **no open-source project combines fitment/compatibility search with a storefront** — every fitment feature anywhere (dedicated automotive tools or bolted onto Magento/WooCommerce/PrestaShop/BigCommerce) is a hand-populated Year/Make/Model/Engine join table, because real fitment data (TecDoc/ACES-PIES) is licensed closed data, not software a platform can ship. Narrows the platform-choice ticket (#329) to two live candidates: **Spree** (Ruby/Rails, BSD-3-Clause, free-tier multi-warehouse + multi-vendor `seller_id` primitives mapping directly onto "N suppliers with markup", first-party Meilisearch — but a new Rails runtime in an all-TypeScript monorepo) vs **Vendure** (TypeScript, GPLv3 core + paid commercial license, same runtime as the rest of this repo, an exact-fit pricing-override hook). Saleor/Shopware/Sylius/Bagisto/Medusa have no comparable fitment or multi-vendor story. A from-scratch Astro+DB build is real but narrower than first assumed: it could reuse `packages/shop-catalog`/`@podbor/i18n`/`site-kit`, not `packages/lead-crm`'s storage layer, and still needs a fresh Postgres + search engine regardless. **Recommendation: don't build a commerce platform from scratch — narrow #329 to Spree vs Vendure.** Fitment/VIN logic is custom either way, platform choice doesn't change that. Also found and reused a thorough prior unmerged research pass (`docs/research/platform-survey.md`, branch `research/platform-survey`, written under stale issue numbers #293/#291 from an earlier session) rather than redoing it from scratch. Full findings in `docs/research/parts-shop-opensource-landscape.md` on branch `research/parts-shop-opensource-landscape`.
- [Research: VIN-decode service options](https://github.com/Zikrasoft/approved_rs/issues/325): **NHTSA vPIC is not viable** — live-tested against a real BMW VIN, it resolved only WMI/plant and failed structurally on model/engine/trim (its check-digit/model-year rules are North-America-specific). Open-source ISO 3779/3780 libraries (`vininfo`, `vin-decoder`) are WMI-level only — manufacturer/country/plant/year-candidate + checksum, useful as a free validation layer but their own docs list extra engine/trim tables only for AvtoVAZ/Ford AU/Nissan/Opel/Renault, not BMW. Of the paid EU options, **Vincario** (rebranded vindecoder.eu) is strongest — ~48 fields, correctly resolves BMW engine/body/series, 3 free lookups/mo then paid tiers. **Critical finding: none of these, paid or free, reach germsp.ru/ETK depth** (paint code, interior trim, fluid volumes, exact production date) — that lives in OEM EPC/ETK or TecDoc-style systems, not generic VIN-decode APIs. TecAlliance's own material says TecDoc already bundles a VIN/VRM lookup tied to its fitment data (flagged, not deep-dived — overlaps the fitment-data-sourcing ticket). **Recommendation: treat "VIN decode" and "BMW parts-fitment spec" as two separate purchases**, use a free ISO 3779 library for validation now, and resolve the fitment-data ticket first since its answer may make a dedicated VIN-decode subscription redundant. Full comparison in `docs/research/vin-decode-options.md` on branch `research/vin-decode-options`.
- [Research: fitment/TecDoc-like data source options, with pricing](https://github.com/Zikrasoft/approved_rs/issues/324): **TecDoc** gives aftermarket fitment + OE cross-refs by KType but only coarse matching (gearbox/steering-dependent parts return multiple candidates) and no exploded diagrams; no public price, a regional partner exists (QUANTUM-AutoMARKET, Belgrade) to get a real quote from. **BMW's own AOS portal** has the full OEM catalogue/diagrams free, but it's a human tool not a data feed, and its terms suggest an EEA/Switzerland company requirement that likely excludes a Serbian company (unverified). **Parts-Catalogs.com is the only vendor with public reseller pricing for OEM diagrams including BMW** (EUR 229-1,299/mo by volume), with a REST API/widget and a 2-day demo — but its data provenance/rights are undisclosed. Laximo has good OEM data but is Russia-based/RUB-billed, logistically awkward for a Serbian company. The Intercars API (#323) carries no fitment/cross-reference data at all, only a TecDoc-ID mapping alongside stock/price — complements TecDoc, doesn't replace it. ACES/PIES is the wrong standard (US/CA/MX, no bundled fitment data, $2,500-12,075/yr). germsp.ru-style sites disclose no data source; Russian practitioners typically combine Laximo + TecDoc as two separate paid services (scraping is also acknowledged as common in that market, not a path to recommend here). **Recommendation: get a scoped quote from QUANTUM-AutoMARKET for TecDoc, in parallel prototype Parts-Catalogs.com against real BMW VINs (B47/B48/N47/N20 engine codes) while confirming their BMW data rights in writing, use Intercars only for price/stock, skip ACES/PIES and scraper-based options, and fall back to manual staff lookup if TecDoc pricing doesn't pencil out at pilot scale.** Full comparison in `docs/research/fitment-data-sourcing.md` on branch `research/fitment-data-sourcing`.

- [Domain-model the part identity & cross-reference model across N suppliers](https://github.com/Zikrasoft/approved_rs/issues/327): **the canonical unit is `Part`** — one interchangeability position (e.g. "oil filter, BMW B47/B48"), never a single brand's number; the OEM number and every aftermarket equivalent sit under one `Part`. Every number is a `PartIdentifier` keyed on the compound `(type, brand, value)` — `oem` / `manufacturer-number` / `ean` — brand mandatory even when unknown (`generic`), so two manufacturers reusing the same string never collide. A supplier's own article id is **not** a `PartIdentifier` — it lives on `SupplierOffer`, scoped to one specific brand-variant, so the same Part sold under two brands by one supplier is two separate purchasable lines at two different prices, never one button hiding a staff pick. Rejected: OEM-number-only canonical key (kills non-OEM-stocked inventory as a dead end), one-Part-per-brand with no shared parent (kills fast "find everything that fits" lookups), supplier-sku-as-a-fourth-identifier-type (duplicates what `SupplierOffer` already is). Full rationale in [ADR-0035](https://github.com/Zikrasoft/approved_rs/blob/main/docs/adr/0035-part-identity-one-canonical-part-brand-keyed-identifiers.md), terms in the repo's first [`GLOSSARY.md`](https://github.com/Zikrasoft/approved_rs/blob/main/GLOSSARY.md), both in [PR #333](https://github.com/Zikrasoft/approved_rs/pull/333) (not merged). **Explicitly deferred, not solved here:** the Vehicle/fitment-position side — spun out as [Domain-model the Vehicle/fitment-position entity](https://github.com/Zikrasoft/approved_rs/issues/334), which also reverses part of ADR-0028.

**All 5 research tickets plus the part-identity ticket are now resolved.** Remaining open work on this map: [Task: get real Intercars API docs/sandbox access](https://github.com/Zikrasoft/approved_rs/issues/328) (unblocked, owner/business-side), [platform choice](https://github.com/Zikrasoft/approved_rs/issues/329) (unblocked), [pilot scope sharpening](https://github.com/Zikrasoft/approved_rs/issues/330) (unblocked), [Domain-model the Vehicle/fitment-position entity](https://github.com/Zikrasoft/approved_rs/issues/334) (unblocked, new); [multi-warehouse pricing UX](https://github.com/Zikrasoft/approved_rs/issues/331) still waits on the platform choice, and [admin fitment-curation workflow](https://github.com/Zikrasoft/approved_rs/issues/332) still waits on the new Vehicle/fitment ticket.

## Not yet specified

- Typesense hosting (self-host vs Cloud) and the sync pipeline from whichever commerce platform gets picked — depends on the platform-choice ticket.
- Delivery mechanics within Serbia (carrier, zones, cost) — deliberately vague, it's a fast-follow.
- Online payment integration specifics (checkout flow shape, webhook/order-status mapping) — depends on the platform choice and the PSP research.
- Admin roles/RBAC beyond owner + 1-2 staff — revisit if the team grows.
- Per-category/per-brand markup granularity beyond the per-supplier % — fast-follow if ever needed.
- Catalog expansion beyond the BMW/German-2-liter pilot (other brands, other part categories) once the pilot proves out.
- Typesense indexing schema specifics (how a `Part` with several `PartIdentifier`s and `SupplierOffer`s becomes one or more search documents) — the identity model is settled (#327), only the index shape is still open, and likely falls out of the platform-choice ticket.

## Out of scope

Nothing yet. The owner chose "full spec for the whole product" as this map's destination (not an MVP-only spec), so nothing from the original 13-point brief has been ruled beyond it — every point is in scope, sequenced via the fast-follow markers above rather than excluded.
